tonight.headline: 17.0–17.8 on a three-hour-old snapshot — the scoreboard in this brief is not the scoreboard.
body: Treat these two numbers as unreliable. The league file behind them was published at 19:07 UTC and has not been rewritten in three hours; the Jacksonville, Denver and 20:25 games have all been played or half-played since. Trevor Lawrence and Jason Myers both show no score here and both have played.

What is real: you still have Jonathan Taylor and Rashee Rice in Kansas City at 18:20 your time, and Matthew Stafford on the bench for Monday night. KEI returns still have Jaxson Dart, De'Von Achane, Cam Skattebo, George Pickens, Tyler Warren and Parker Washington to come — six live starters against your two. The 34% is probably closer to right than the 17.0 is.

case.label: Why the number is wrong and the shape may not be
case.body: Cross-checking against the Chem file, which published at 21:52 and scores receptions and receiving yards identically to this league — the fourteen scoring items that differ between the two are all quarterback, kicking and defensive — Garrett Wilson is at 16.7 rather than 5.3 and Matthew Golden at 9.8 rather than 1.8. That is roughly 19 points this brief cannot show you. It does not fix the matchup: KEI returns have six starters left to your two.

case.label: What you actually control
case.body: Nothing in the lineup. Every Bloodsports player except Taylor, Rice and Stafford is locked, Taylor and Rice are already starting, and Lawrence is locked at quarterback so Stafford cannot come in. The one move worth making is a defence swap that has to wait for rosters to unlock.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Taylor-and-Rice night in Kansas City. Rice ran an 8% target share in Week 1 — 17 targetless routes before a red-zone screen — and Pro Football Network still have him WR8 this week with Mahomes throwing. That thesis resolves at 18:20 your time, which is after this brief was written.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: When the week rolls · free agent, no priority
doFirst.title: Drop the Ravens D/ST for the Giants D/ST the moment rosters unlock
doFirst.subtitle: New York are 2nd for Week 3 against Tennessee, Baltimore 16th at Dallas — and the Giants are a FREE AGENT here at 2.9% rostered, so this costs no waiver priority.

case.label: The board turned
case.body: Draft Sharks' Week 3 defence rankings, fetched this run: Carolina 1st at Cleveland, New York Giants 2nd against Tennessee, Detroit 3rd, Green Bay 6th, New England 9th, Cleveland 14th, Baltimore 16th at Dallas, Chicago 17th, the Rams 22nd. Baltimore have been 3rd of 32 on FantasyPros for ten straight runs of this brief and nothing free here was close. That is over.

case.label: Why it costs nothing
case.body: The Giants D/ST carries status FREEAGENT in this snapshot at 2.9% national ownership. IPADE priority never resets and Bloodsports sit 3rd of 10, which is the single asset this brief keeps refusing to spend — STRATEGY section 6 forbids a claim on a defence outright. A free agent is not a claim. The rule and the move do not collide.

case.label: Why it waits
case.body: The Ravens defence has already played and banked its points in this week's scoring; dropping it now throws those away to chase a Giants game that has not kicked off. The right execution is Tuesday, when rosters unlock and Week 2 is closed. That is also why this is not an ELITE card.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Another manager takes the Giants first — they are free to all ten and this snapshot is three hours old, so the status may already be wrong. Check it before you act. Green Bay at 6th are on waivers here and would cost priority, so the real fallback is the Rams D/ST, free at 87.6% rostered but only 22nd for Week 3, in which case hold Baltimore and stream in Week 4.

action.label: Add Giants D/ST · drop Ravens D/ST

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · when the week rolls
doFirst.title: MarShawn Lloyd for Matthew Golden in the flex — unarmed, and it should stay that way
doFirst.subtitle: Your flex scored 1.8 and Lloyd scored 10.4 from the bench. Published so the seat is a considered one, not because one week is a role change.

case.label: What the week said
case.body: Golden 1.8 in the flex against Lloyd's 10.4 and Tuten's 12.9 on the bench — the Tuten figure read from the Chem file, because this league's snapshot is three hours old and still shows him blank. On the afternoon alone the flex was the wrong body.

case.label: Why it stays unarmed
case.body: Golden's seat was won on role, not on a result: 12 targets and a 30% target share in Week 1 with Jordan Love throwing 42 times to 21 handoffs. STRATEGY section 8 says weeks 1–3 are noise and to react to role news only, never to box scores. Nothing in Green Bay's usage changed today — he had a quiet game in the same role.

case.label: What Lloyd has going for him
case.body: Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List, placed 30 August, and Lloyd is first in line for that vacancy. 10.4 today at 77.4% rostered. His case is a vacated role, which is STRATEGY section 4's second-strongest signal — it just has not overtaken a 30% target share yet.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Two straight weeks of Golden under a 15% target share, or Green Bay handing Lloyd the early-down work outright. Either fires this the moment rosters unlock. One 1.8 does not.

whatWentWrong.title: This league's publisher stopped three hours ago and nobody told you
whatWentWrong.lead: league-1325565673.json was last written at 19:07 UTC. The Chem file was written at 21:52. The commit history shows this file being rewritten every 15 to 30 minutes all afternoon and then nothing.

case.label: How I know
case.body: The repository's commit log for this file: 15:07, 15:37, 16:07, 16:37, 16:52, 17:22, 17:52, 19:07 — and then a three-hour gap while the other league kept publishing. This is not a slow refresh, it is a stopped one.

case.label: What it costs you
case.body: Trevor Lawrence and Jason Myers both show no score and both have played. Garrett Wilson shows 5.3 where the fresher file has 16.7; Golden shows 1.8 against 9.8. Roughly nineteen points of your own scoring is missing from the matchup panel, and Bhayshul Tuten's 12.9 is missing from the flex comparison.

case.label: What it changes in this brief
case.body: It is the reason the Giants defence card is a WHEN_UNLOCKED instruction rather than something to fire now: his FREEAGENT status is a three-hour-old reading, and a free agent at 2.9% ownership can be taken in that time. Verify in ESPN before you act.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A publish appearing with a timestamp inside the last thirty minutes. If the next run still sees 19:07 on this file, the Cloud Function needs restarting and the brief should say so louder than it analyses.

whatWentWrong.title: Your defence was held for ten runs and Baltimore lost
whatWentWrong.lead: The Ravens D/ST shows 6 in this snapshot, taken mid-game, in a loss to New Orleans. They are 16th for Week 3 at Dallas.

case.label: The hold was well-argued
case.body: FantasyPros had Baltimore 3rd of 32 against a New Orleans line that gave up five first-half sacks in Week 1 with Tyler Shough throwing. The Rams, free here at 87.6% rostered, were not close. On the morning's information the hold was right and it was right for ten runs.

case.label: The clause that tripped
case.body: 'Baltimore finish outside the top 12 defensive scores in Week 2.' A 6 taken before the fourth quarter in a game Baltimore lost is not going to survive that bar, and the Chem file's fresher reading of the same defence — on that league's different defensive scoring — is 3.0.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It fires the Giants card above, and it does it without touching waiver priority, which is the part that matters in this league. The second half of the thesis — never spend priority on a defence — is untouched and stays on the record.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore outscoring the Giants in Week 3. Dallas are not a soft draw for a defence and Tennessee are; if that inverts, this was a stream that cost a roster move for nothing.

whatWentWrong.title: Your flex scored 1.8 and two bench players beat it by eight and eleven
whatWentWrong.lead: Matthew Golden 1.8, MarShawn Lloyd 10.4, Bhayshul Tuten 12.9. Golden has held that flex seat since 15 September on a 30% target share.

case.label: Why Golden has the seat
case.body: Week 1: 12 targets, a 30% target share, six catches for 95 yards and two red-zone looks, with Jordan Love throwing 42 times to 21 handoffs. DraftKings had him a start. That is a role read, and role reads are what this brief is supposed to run on.

case.label: What today does not tell you
case.body: Whether the role changed. A 1.8 can come from four targets or from twelve with drops, and the target count for today's Green Bay game is not in a three-hour-old file and had not published anywhere I could reach. Chasing the points without the targets is chasing last week's box score.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It puts the comparison on the board as an unarmed card so that Tuesday's run inherits it instead of rediscovering it. It does not move the flex.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Golden's Week 2 target count, once it publishes. Under six targets on top of today's 1.8 is the beginning of a role change; ten targets and one bad afternoon is just variance.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +40.6 across the season against your +11.6 — three and a half times yours, and saying so is the only thing that gets this message read.

case.label: The structural surplus
case.body: Re-verified against the 19:07 snapshot rather than carried: Lamar Jackson is still slot 20, behind Josh Allen at slot 0, in a one-quarterback league. Team 13 score exactly zero from him every week. Their second starting running back is still Rachaad White at slot 2 on a 7.6 projection, and Washington's Week 1 backfield snaps were Croskey-Merritt 33, White 27, Kaytron Allen 6 of 67. Tuten fixes a hole they actually have.

case.label: The honest risk, and it got worse today
case.body: Both sides of this are priced on seasonProj, and this run proved seasonProj is frozen: 251 players compared between the 15:07Z and 19:07Z copies of this file, and not one season number moved while twelve weekly projections did. The +11.6 and +40.6 are August's opinion, not today's. On this week's projection the same trade is +3.4 me, +0.3 them.

case.label: Why it is still worth having on the board
case.body: Because the structure is not a projection. A bench quarterback in a one-QB league scores nobody anything, whatever the number attached to him, and that is true in August and in December. Do not re-send it — this manager has ignored three offers. Respond if they open.

case.label: The better version to push on a counter
case.body: Matthew Golden for Lamar scores +26.5 me and +12.2 them — more than twice this one's gain to you and still positive for them. It is not the standing offer because it gives them a third of the upgrade, but it is the direction to steer any counter.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second real running back, which kills their +40.6. Or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Rachaad White is dropped or benched, which removes the evidence. Lamar is not on a Baltimore injury report — he threw for 12.9 in this file's scoring today in a loss.

trades.sources: Draft Sharks · RotoWire · GitHub commit history · ESPN
trades.copyText: Hi — would you do Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson? You're carrying Lamar behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he scores you nothing every week, and Tuten slots straight in next to McCaffrey ahead of Rachaad White, who was second in Washington's backfield on snaps in Week 1. On ESPN's season numbers it's about +40 for you and +12 for me — it's the better side of the deal for you and I'd rather say that than have you work it out and wonder why I didn't.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +15.5 against your +4.7 — more than three times yours, because they are starting Baker Mayfield with no backup quarterback at all.

case.label: Their hole
case.body: Re-verified structurally against this snapshot: Metcalf Gala start Baker Mayfield at slot 0 on a 259.0 season projection and carry no second quarterback. Mayfield scored 6.3 today. Waddle is still slot 20, behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Mike Evans at slot 4 and Chris Olave in the flex — he is their fourth receiver and he does not play.

case.label: Your side of it
case.body: Stafford is your backup quarterback behind Trevor Lawrence and has started no week for you. Waddle would enter the flex. You keep a starting quarterback and convert a bench arm into a player who plays, which is the consolidation STRATEGY section 7 asks for.

case.label: The weakness, stated plainly
case.body: Four searches last run and two this run produced nothing on Waddle's target share in Denver — every result was either Miami-era or a Week 2 preview. His 11.1 today (read from the Chem file, where receiving scores identically) is one data point in a new offence. The 214.3 season projection behind the +4.7 is frozen August output, now measured and confirmed frozen this run.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Metcalf Gala acquire or start a second quarterback, which removes the upgrade they are buying. Or Waddle's Week 2 target count publishes under five, which says a receiver on a new team has not found a role. Or the frozen seasonProj is taken at face value, in which case this reduces to a roughly one-point weekly flex gain and sits right on STRATEGY's floor.

trades.sources: Denver Gazette · Pro Football Network · GitHub commit history · ESPN
trades.copyText: Hi — interested in Matthew Stafford for Jaylen Waddle? You're one Mayfield injury from having no quarterback at all, and Waddle is your WR4 behind St. Brown, Evans and Olave, so he isn't scoring you anything most weeks. On ESPN's season numbers it's about +15 for you and +5 for me. Happy to look at a different receiver if Waddle's not the one you want to move.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: Nine targets and 7/88/1 with Flowers out — and in this league he is not worth the priority.

case.label: The role
case.body: Nine targets, seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown at New Orleans without Zay Flowers (NBC Sports, today). Baltimore are also without Ja'Kobi Lane, who fractured a wrist, and Devontez Walker with a groin. His ownership moved +8.02 in a day, the biggest single move on this board.

case.label: Why the two leagues answer this differently
case.body: He is on WAIVERS here, clearing Wednesday 01:00 your time, and IPADE priority never resets. Bloodsports are 3rd of 10 and section 6 says spend that only on a player who starts immediately or a genuine league-winner. A receiver on one nine-target game with two team-mates hurt is neither. In Chem, where priority resets weekly, the same player is a Do-first claim — and that asymmetry is the point.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If he clears unclaimed on Wednesday and reverts to free agency, take him then for nothing, with the drop being Hockenson once his seat reopens on 27 September. If Flowers returns in Week 3 and Bateman's share collapses, this row closes at no cost.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: A free agent here at 76.5% rostered nationally — no priority, only a roster move. Still unresolved.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on this wire, status FREEAGENT. The thumb cleared and NBC had him active at Denver, with Riley Moss covering him while Patrick Surtain II took Brian Thomas Jr. — the softer half of Denver's coverage.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: Every seat on this bench is closed by the seven-day churn rule: Vele came in 17 September, Stafford 19 September, Hockenson this morning. There is no droppable body, and Jacksonville's box score from this afternoon had not published anywhere I could reach.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Thursday 24 September, when Vele's seat reopens, if Meyers's Denver target count came in ahead of Brian Thomas Jr.'s and Vele has not repeated his 17.3% share. He is free, so this costs priority nothing and can wait for the box score.

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: TE11 and free here, which matters in the one league whose flex takes a tight end.

case.label: Why he is on this list at all
case.body: 167.4 season projection, 81.1% rostered nationally, status FREEAGENT — no priority at stake. IPADE's flex takes a tight end, which STRATEGY section 9 says makes a second startable TE genuinely valuable here and worthless in Chem.

case.label: Why the answer is still no
case.body: You already carry two tight ends and added the second one this morning. Loveland is TE2 on consensus rank with 100% of Chicago's third downs in Week 1; Hockenson came in at 06:26 today and his seat is closed until 27 September. Adding a third would be the one-seat-three-players pattern section 3 exists to stop.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Caleb Williams's hamstring costs him time and Loveland's role goes with it — Ben Johnson expects clarity Monday. Ferguson is free, so there is no cost to waiting for that news.

doNotChase.name: Rico Dowdle
doNotChase.lead: This morning's watch row, closed by two things that both happened this afternoon.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He exited in the second quarter with a toe, came back after half, and was ruled out: 7 carries for 22 yards and 2 catches for 22 (NBC Sports, Yahoo). That is a re-aggravation of a toe that was already a recurring problem, with no timeline attached.

case.label: The other thing that changed
case.body: He is no longer a free agent. This morning's row rested on him having cleared waivers unclaimed at 01:00, so 'the price objection is gone'. The Sunday slate put him back on WAIVERS, clearing Wednesday 07:00Z — so claiming him now would spend never-resetting priority on an injured committee back, which is exactly what section 6 forbids.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: He clears Wednesday unclaimed and reverts to free agency, and Pittsburgh's Wednesday practice report has him full. Both of those, not one. Until then the correct read is the one the previous run got right on the claim and wrong on the player: good back, wrong price.

doNotChase.sources: NBC Sports · Yahoo Sports · CBS Sports · ESPN

doNotChase.name: Cam Little
doNotChase.lead: Free at 87.5% rostered, a marginally better Week 3 draw, and still the wrong move.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Draft Sharks have Jacksonville's kicker 8th for Week 3 at home to New England and Seattle's 9th at Washington. That is one place. STRATEGY section 10 says do not propose a move worth under a point, and a one-rank kicker difference is well under one.

case.label: Why he keeps coming back
case.body: He is the name the owner dropped on 18 September to add Myers, and he is free, so he resurfaces at the top of every board. Re-adding him would also rebuild the Jacksonville concentration section 8 flags for the Week 7 bye, when Tuten, the Jaguars D/ST and Little were all out together.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty kickers in Week 2 — which this snapshot cannot tell you, because Seattle kicked after it was written. The kicker seat reopens 25 September and the answer then is whoever tops the board, as a free agent, never as a claim.

doNotChase.sources: Draft Sharks · Pro Football Network · ESPN

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: The other kicker the board keeps surfacing, and this week he is on waivers.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Draft Sharks have Minnesota's kicker 12th for Week 3 at Tampa Bay, behind Seattle's 9th. He was PFN's K5 for Week 2 and free; he is now on WAIVERS clearing Wednesday, so he would cost never-resetting priority to move from 9th to 12th. That is the worst version of this trade.

case.label: Why he was ever a candidate
case.body: Minnesota's kicker has been a top-five weekly name on two published boards this month, and he was a free agent as recently as yesterday. The ownership band and the ranking were both real; the Week 3 draw is not.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Minnesota getting a quarterback back — Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and Carson Wentz has started twice — which would lift the implied team total the kicker ranking rests on. And him reverting to free agency, because no kicker is worth this league's priority.
